citations.F1: N+1: `serialize_event` runs one `users` lookup per event, awaited sequentially (~1k round trips per request); fetch all distinct actor_ids in one `WHERE id = ANY($1)`.
citations.F2: `seen` is a list, so dedupe is O(n²) with `in`; use a set
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` calls synchronous `requests.get` inside an async handler, freezing the worker's event loop up to 2 s per uncached IP
citations.F4: Missing index: nothing serves `WHERE org_id AND created_at >= ORDER BY created_at DESC`, hence 1.4 s per call; `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_id_created_at_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` is appended on every request and never trimmed (~120 req/s × 20 h ≈ 8.6M floats per worker, ×4 workers), and `/internal/metrics` sorts the whole list on the loop each call; replace with a bounded deque or a histogram.
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded per-worker dict keyed by client IP; bound it (LRU + TTL).
citations.F8: Confirm before touching code: `py-spy dump` an api worker mid-request (expect it parked in `requests.get`), and `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` the events query with acme's params (expect Seq Scan over 4.2M rows).
citations.F9: Do not ship the proposal: 16 workers × 50 conns × 6 pods is 4,800 Postgres connections, 4× more copies of the per-worker leak, and a 60 s Redis cache hides the bug without stopping the event-loop stalls
